headline: Medium risk: dbt-core can leak warehouse data into Prefect workflows, while Prefect’s broad egress raises downstream compliance and data-handling concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No documented shared communication channel, clipboard bridge, or parser relationship exists between dbt-core and Prefect in the provided profiles. dbt-core only calls data warehouse APIs, and Prefect only calls GitHub APIs; neither profile shows ingestion of the other’s outputs as instructions.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between dbt-core and Prefect, reassess prompt-injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy raw outputs between them.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging if a shared channel is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data and has allowlisted network egress; Prefect has broad egress and can call external APIs. Even without a shared workspace documented, a workflow that passes dbt outputs into Prefect could expose warehouse data beyond the original boundary.
conditions: IF dbt-core outputs containing warehouse data are handed to Prefect tasks, leakage risk is present.
IF Prefect is configured to transmit task payloads to external services, sensitive data exposure increases.
mitigations: Minimize payloads passed from dbt-core to Prefect.
Redact warehouse fields before orchestration.
Restrict Prefect task logging.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class filtering at the handoff boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering tools, but the profiles show no overlapping write surface such as shared filesystem, git state, or mutable OAuth scopes. dbt-core only calls a data warehouse, while Prefect calls GitHub APIs, so direct write contention is not evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory or repository, write conflicts become plausible.
IF either agent gains write access to the same warehouse objects, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Serialize any shared-resource updates.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Prefect is an orchestration tool, so dbt-core outputs can become Prefect inputs in a default workflow. If Prefect treats dbt-produced artifacts or metadata as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream automation even though no direct evidence of such verification exists.
conditions: IF Prefect consumes dbt artifacts without validation, cascading errors are possible.
IF Prefect triggers downstream actions from dbt status or metadata, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add validation steps before orchestration.
Require schema checks on dbt outputs.
Gate downstream actions on explicit approval.
Log and review failed transformations.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between dbt and Prefect.

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch or regulated-data certification gap, but a compliance issue can arise if warehouse data is routed through Prefect logs or external API calls without retention controls.
conditions: IF warehouse data is included in Prefect logs or task payloads, retention and residency controls must be reviewed.
IF the deployment handles regulated data, the pair should be rechecked against the applicable policy.
mitigations: Disable verbose task logging.
Exclude sensitive fields from orchestration metadata.
Set short log retention.
Review data-flow diagrams before deployment.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls across both systems.
